10.description: The catalog pg_aggregate stores information about aggregate functions. An aggregate function is a function that operates on a set of values (typically one column from each row that matches a query condition) and returns a single value computed from all these values. Typical aggregate functions are sum, count, and max. Each entry in pg_aggregate is an extension of an entry in pg_proc. The pg_proc entry carries the aggregate's name, input and output data types, and other information that is similar to ordinary functions.

columns.name: aggfnoid

columns.name: aggkind
columns.description: Aggregate kind: n for normal aggregates, o for ordered-set aggregates, or h for hypothetical-set aggregates

columns.name: aggnumdirectargs
columns.description: Number of direct (non-aggregated) arguments of an ordered-set or hypothetical-set aggregate, counting a variadic array as one argument. If equal to pronargs, the aggregate must be variadic and the variadic array describes the aggregated arguments as well as the final direct arguments. Always zero for normal aggregates.

19b.description: The catalog pg_aggregate stores information about aggregate functions. An aggregate function is a function that operates on a set of values (typically one column from each row that matches a query condition) and returns a single value computed from all these values. Typical aggregate functions are sum, count, and max. Each entry in pg_aggregate is an extension of an entry in pg_proc. The pg_proc entry carries the aggregate's name, input and output data types, and other information that is similar to ordinary functions.

18.description: The pg_aios view lists all handles that are currently in-use. An I/O handle is used to reference an I/O operation that is being prepared, executed or is in the process of completing. pg_aios contains one row for each I/O handle.

columns.name: pid
columns.description: Process ID of the server process that is issuing this I/O.

columns.name: io_id
columns.description: Identifier of the I/O handle. Handles are reused once the I/O completed (or if the handle is released before I/O is started). On reuse pg_aios.io_generation is incremented.

columns.name: io_generation
columns.description: Generation of the I/O handle.

columns.name: state
columns.description: State of the I/O handle: HANDED_OUT, referenced by code but not yet used

columns.name: operation
columns.description: Operation performed using the I/O handle: invalid, not yet known

columns.name: off
columns.description: Offset of the I/O operation.

columns.name: length
columns.description: Length of the I/O operation.

columns.name: target
columns.description: What kind of object is the I/O targeting: smgr, I/O on relations

columns.name: handle_data_len
columns.description: Length of the data associated with the I/O operation. For I/O to/from and , this indicates the number of buffers the I/O is operating on.

columns.name: raw_result
columns.description: Low-level result of the I/O operation, or NULL if the operation has not yet completed.

columns.name: result
columns.description: High-level result of the I/O operation: UNKNOWN means that the result of the operation is not yet known.

columns.name: target_desc
columns.description: Description of what the I/O operation is targeting.

columns.name: f_sync
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the I/O is executed synchronously.

columns.name: f_localmem
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the I/O references process local memory.

columns.name: f_buffered
columns.description: Flag indicating whether the I/O is buffered I/O.

10.description: The catalog pg_amop stores information about operators associated with access method operator families. There is one row for each operator that is a member of an operator family. A family member can be either a search operator or an ordering operator. An operator can appear in more than one family, but cannot appear in more than one search position nor more than one ordering position within a family. (It is allowed, though unlikely, for an operator to be used for both search and ordering purposes.)

columns.description: Operator strategy number

columns.name: amoppurpose
columns.description: Operator purpose, either s for search or o for ordering

columns.name: amopmethod
columns.description: Index access method operator family is for

columns.description: The B-tree operator family this entry sorts according to, if an ordering operator; zero if a search operator

10.description: The catalog pg_attribute stores information about table columns. There will be exactly one pg_attribute row for every column in every table in the database. (There will also be attribute entries for indexes, and indeed all objects that have pg_class entries.)

columns.name: attrelid
columns.description: The table this column belongs to

columns.name: attname
columns.description: The column name

columns.name: atttypid
columns.description: The data type of this column

columns.name: attstattarget
columns.description: attstattarget controls the level of detail of statistics accumulated for this column by . A zero value indicates that no statistics should be collected. A negative value says to use the system default statistics target. The exact meaning of positive values is data type-dependent. For scalar data types, attstattarget is both the target number of most common values to collect, and the target number of histogram bins to create.

columns.name: attlen
columns.description: A copy of pg_type.typlen of this column's type

columns.name: attnum
columns.description: The number of the column. Ordinary columns are numbered from 1 up. System columns, such as oid, have (arbitrary) negative numbers.

columns.name: attndims
columns.description: Number of dimensions, if the column is an array type; otherwise 0. (Presently, the number of dimensions of an array is not enforced, so any nonzero value effectively means it's an array.)

columns.name: attcacheoff
columns.description: Always -1 in storage, but when loaded into a row descriptor in memory this might be updated to cache the offset of the attribute within the row

columns.name: atttypmod
columns.description: atttypmod records type-specific data supplied at table creation time (for example, the maximum length of a varchar column). It is passed to type-specific input functions and length coercion functions. The value will generally be -1 for types that do not need atttypmod.

columns.name: attbyval
columns.description: A copy of pg_type.typbyval of this column's type

columns.name: attstorage
columns.description: Normally a copy of pg_type.typstorage of this column's type. For TOAST-able data types, this can be altered after column creation to control storage policy.

columns.name: attalign
columns.description: A copy of pg_type.typalign of this column's type

columns.name: attnotnull
columns.description: This represents a not-null constraint.

columns.name: atthasdef
columns.description: This column has a default value, in which case there will be a corresponding entry in the pg_attrdef catalog that actually defines the value.

columns.name: attidentity
columns.description: If a zero byte (''), then not an identity column. Otherwise, a = generated always, d = generated by default.

columns.name: attisdropped
columns.description: This column has been dropped and is no longer valid. A dropped column is still physically present in the table, but is ignored by the parser and so cannot be accessed via SQL.

columns.name: attislocal
columns.description: This column is defined locally in the relation. Note that a column can be locally defined and inherited simultaneously.

columns.name: attinhcount
columns.description: The number of direct ancestors this column has. A column with a nonzero number of ancestors cannot be dropped nor renamed.

columns.name: attcollation
columns.description: The defined collation of the column, or zero if the column is not of a collatable data type.

columns.name: attacl
columns.description: Column-level access privileges, if any have been granted specifically on this column

columns.name: attoptions
columns.description: Attribute-level options, as keyword=value strings

columns.name: attfdwoptions
columns.description: Attribute-level foreign data wrapper options, as keyword=value strings

10.description: The catalog pg_authid contains information about database authorization identifiers (roles). A role subsumes the concepts of users and groups. A user is essentially just a role with the rolcanlogin flag set. Any role (with or without rolcanlogin) can have other roles as members; see pg_auth_members.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: rolname
columns.description: Role name

columns.name: rolsuper
columns.description: Role has superuser privileges

columns.name: rolinherit
columns.description: Role automatically inherits privileges of roles it is a member of

columns.name: rolcreaterole
columns.description: Role can create more roles

columns.name: rolcreatedb
columns.description: Role can create databases

columns.name: rolcanlogin
columns.description: Role can log in. That is, this role can be given as the initial session authorization identifier.

columns.name: rolreplication
columns.description: Role is a replication role. A replication role can initiate replication connections and create and drop replication slots.

columns.name: rolbypassrls
columns.description: Role bypasses every row level security policy, see for more information.

columns.name: rolconnlimit
columns.description: For roles that can log in, this sets maximum number of concurrent connections this role can make. -1 means no limit.

columns.name: rolpassword
columns.description: Password (possibly encrypted); null if none. The format depends on the form of encryption used.

columns.name: rolvaliduntil
columns.description: Password expiry time (only used for password authentication); null if no expiration

10.description: The catalog pg_cast stores data type conversion paths, both built-in and user-defined.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: castsource
columns.description: OID of the source data type

columns.name: casttarget
columns.description: OID of the target data type

columns.name: castfunc
columns.description: The OID of the function to use to perform this cast. Zero is stored if the cast method doesn't require a function.

columns.name: castcontext
columns.description: Indicates what contexts the cast can be invoked in. e means only as an explicit cast (using CAST or :: syntax). a means implicitly in assignment to a target column, as well as explicitly. i means implicitly in expressions, as well as the other cases.

columns.name: castmethod
columns.description: Indicates how the cast is performed. f means that the function specified in the castfunc field is used. i means that the input/output functions are used. b means that the types are binary-coercible, thus no conversion is required.

10.description: The catalog pg_class catalogs tables and most everything else that has columns or is otherwise similar to a table. This includes indexes (but see also pg_index), sequences (but see also pg_sequence), views, materialized views, composite types, and TOAST tables; see relkind. Below, when we mean all of these kinds of objects we speak of relations. Not all columns are meaningful for all relation types.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: relname
columns.description: Name of the table, index, view, etc.

columns.name: relnamespace
columns.description: The OID of the namespace that contains this relation

columns.name: reltype
columns.description: The OID of the data type that corresponds to this table's row type, if any (zero for indexes, which have no pg_type entry)

columns.name: reloftype
columns.description: For typed tables, the OID of the underlying composite type, zero for all other relations

columns.name: relowner
columns.description: Owner of the relation

columns.name: relam
columns.description: If this is an index, the access method used (B-tree, hash, etc.)

columns.name: relfilenode
columns.description: Name of the on-disk file of this relation; zero means this is a mapped relation whose disk file name is determined by low-level state

columns.name: reltablespace
columns.description: The tablespace in which this relation is stored. If zero, the database's default tablespace is implied. (Not meaningful if the relation has no on-disk file.)

columns.name: relpages
columns.description: Size of the on-disk representation of this table in pages (of size BLCKSZ). This is only an estimate used by the planner. It is updated by VACUUM, ANALYZE, and a few DDL commands such as CREATE INDEX.

columns.name: reltuples
columns.description: Number of rows in the table. This is only an estimate used by the planner. It is updated by VACUUM, ANALYZE, and a few DDL commands such as CREATE INDEX.

columns.name: relallvisible
columns.description: Number of pages that are marked all-visible in the table's visibility map. This is only an estimate used by the planner. It is updated by VACUUM, ANALYZE, and a few DDL commands such as CREATE INDEX.

columns.name: reltoastrelid
columns.description: OID of the TOAST table associated with this table, 0 if none. The TOAST table stores large attributes out of line in a secondary table.

columns.name: relhasindex
columns.description: True if this is a table and it has (or recently had) any indexes

columns.name: relisshared
columns.description: True if this table is shared across all databases in the cluster. Only certain system catalogs (such as pg_database) are shared.

columns.name: relpersistence
columns.description: p = permanent table, u = unlogged table, t = temporary table

columns.name: relkind
columns.description: r = ordinary table, i = index, S = sequence, t = TOAST table, v = view, m = materialized view, c = composite type, f = foreign table, p = partitioned table

columns.name: relnatts
columns.description: Number of user columns in the relation (system columns not counted). There must be this many corresponding entries in pg_attribute. See also pg_attribute.attnum.

columns.name: relchecks
columns.description: Number of CHECK constraints on the table; see pg_constraint catalog

columns.name: relhasoids
columns.description: True if we generate an OID for each row of the relation

columns.name: relhaspkey
columns.description: True if the table has (or once had) a primary key

columns.name: relhasrules
columns.description: True if table has (or once had) rules; see pg_rewrite catalog

columns.name: relhastriggers
columns.description: True if table has (or once had) triggers; see pg_trigger catalog

columns.name: relhassubclass
columns.description: True if table has (or once had) any inheritance children

columns.name: relrowsecurity
columns.description: True if table has row level security enabled; see pg_policy catalog

columns.name: relforcerowsecurity
columns.description: True if row level security (when enabled) will also apply to table owner; see pg_policy catalog

columns.name: relispopulated
columns.description: True if relation is populated (this is true for all relations other than some materialized views)

columns.name: relreplident
columns.description: Columns used to form replica identity for rows: d = default (primary key, if any), n = nothing, f = all columns, i = index with indisreplident set (same as nothing if the index used has been dropped)

columns.name: relispartition
columns.description: True if table is a partition

columns.name: relfrozenxid
columns.description: All transaction IDs before this one have been replaced with a permanent (frozen) transaction ID in this table. This is used to track whether the table needs to be vacuumed in order to prevent transaction ID wraparound or to allow pg_xact to be shrunk. Zero (InvalidTransactionId) if the relation is not a table.

columns.name: relminmxid
columns.description: All multixact IDs before this one have been replaced by a transaction ID in this table. This is used to track whether the table needs to be vacuumed in order to prevent multixact ID wraparound or to allow pg_multixact to be shrunk. Zero (InvalidMultiXactId) if the relation is not a table.

columns.name: relacl
columns.description: Access privileges; see and for details

columns.name: reloptions
columns.description: Access-method-specific options, as keyword=value strings

columns.name: relpartbound
columns.description: If table is a partition (see relispartition), internal representation of the partition bound

10.description: The catalog pg_constraint stores check, primary key, unique, foreign key, and exclusion constraints on tables. (Column constraints are not treated specially. Every column constraint is equivalent to some table constraint.) Not-null constraints are represented in the pg_attribute catalog, not here.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: conname
columns.description: Constraint name (not necessarily unique!)

columns.name: connamespace
columns.description: The OID of the namespace that contains this constraint

columns.name: contype
columns.description: c = check constraint, f = foreign key constraint, p = primary key constraint, u = unique constraint, t = constraint trigger, x = exclusion constraint

columns.name: condeferrable
columns.description: Is the constraint deferrable?

columns.name: condeferred
columns.description: Is the constraint deferred by default?

columns.name: convalidated
columns.description: Has the constraint been validated? Currently, can only be false for foreign keys and CHECK constraints

columns.name: conrelid
columns.description: The table this constraint is on; 0 if not a table constraint

columns.name: contypid
columns.description: The domain this constraint is on; 0 if not a domain constraint

columns.name: conindid
columns.description: The index supporting this constraint, if it's a unique, primary key, foreign key, or exclusion constraint; else 0

columns.name: confrelid
columns.description: If a foreign key, the referenced table; else 0

columns.name: confupdtype
columns.description: Foreign key update action code: a = no action, r = restrict, c = cascade, n = set null, d = set default

columns.name: confdeltype
columns.description: Foreign key deletion action code: a = no action, r = restrict, c = cascade, n = set null, d = set default

columns.name: confmatchtype
columns.description: Foreign key match type: f = full, p = partial, s = simple

columns.name: conislocal
columns.description: This constraint is defined locally for the relation. Note that a constraint can be locally defined and inherited simultaneously.

columns.name: coninhcount
columns.description: The number of direct inheritance ancestors this constraint has. A constraint with a nonzero number of ancestors cannot be dropped nor renamed.

columns.name: connoinherit
columns.description: This constraint is defined locally for the relation. It is a non-inheritable constraint.

columns.name: conkey
columns.description: If a table constraint (including foreign keys, but not constraint triggers), list of the constrained columns

columns.name: confkey
columns.description: If a foreign key, list of the referenced columns

columns.name: conpfeqop
columns.description: If a foreign key, list of the equality operators for PK = FK comparisons

columns.name: conppeqop
columns.description: If a foreign key, list of the equality operators for PK = PK comparisons

columns.name: conffeqop
columns.description: If a foreign key, list of the equality operators for FK = FK comparisons

columns.name: conexclop
columns.description: If an exclusion constraint, list of the per-column exclusion operators

columns.name: conbin
columns.description: If a check constraint, an internal representation of the expression

columns.name: consrc
columns.description: If a check constraint, a human-readable representation of the expression

10.description: The catalog pg_database stores information about the available databases. Databases are created with the command. Consult for details about the meaning of some of the parameters.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: datname
columns.description: Database name

columns.name: datdba
columns.description: Owner of the database, usually the user who created it

columns.name: encoding
columns.description: Character encoding for this database (pg_encoding_to_char() can translate this number to the encoding name)

columns.name: datcollate
columns.description: LC_COLLATE for this database

columns.name: datctype
columns.description: LC_CTYPE for this database

columns.name: datistemplate
columns.description: If true, then this database can be cloned by any user with CREATEDB privileges; if false, then only superusers or the owner of the database can clone it.

columns.name: datallowconn
columns.description: If false then no one can connect to this database. This is used to protect the template0 database from being altered.

columns.name: datconnlimit
columns.description: Sets maximum number of concurrent connections that can be made to this database. -1 means no limit.

columns.name: datlastsysoid
columns.description: Last system OID in the database; useful particularly to pg_dump

columns.name: datfrozenxid
columns.description: All transaction IDs before this one have been replaced with a permanent (frozen) transaction ID in this database. This is used to track whether the database needs to be vacuumed in order to prevent transaction ID wraparound or to allow pg_xact to be shrunk. It is the minimum of the per-table pg_class.relfrozenxid values.

columns.name: datminmxid
columns.description: All multixact IDs before this one have been replaced with a transaction ID in this database. This is used to track whether the database needs to be vacuumed in order to prevent multixact ID wraparound or to allow pg_multixact to be shrunk. It is the minimum of the per-table pg_class.relminmxid values.

columns.name: dattablespace
columns.description: The default tablespace for the database. Within this database, all tables for which pg_class.reltablespace is zero will be stored in this tablespace; in particular, all the non-shared system catalogs will be there.

columns.name: datacl
columns.description: Access privileges; see and for details

columns.name: oid

columns.name: datname
columns.description: Database name

columns.name: datdba
columns.description: Owner of the database, usually the user who created it

columns.name: encoding
columns.description: Character encoding for this database (pg_encoding_to_char() can translate this number to the encoding name)

columns.name: datcollate
columns.description: LC_COLLATE for this database

columns.name: datctype
columns.description: LC_CTYPE for this database

columns.name: datistemplate
columns.description: If true, then this database can be cloned by any user with CREATEDB privileges; if false, then only superusers or the owner of the database can clone it.

columns.name: datallowconn
columns.description: If false then no one can connect to this database. This is used to protect the template0 database from being altered.

columns.name: datconnlimit
columns.description: Sets maximum number of concurrent connections that can be made to this database. -1 means no limit.

columns.name: datlastsysoid
columns.description: Last system OID in the database; useful particularly to pg_dump

columns.name: datfrozenxid
columns.description: All transaction IDs before this one have been replaced with a permanent (frozen) transaction ID in this database. This is used to track whether the database needs to be vacuumed in order to prevent transaction ID wraparound or to allow pg_clog to be shrunk. It is the minimum of the per-table pg_class.relfrozenxid values.

columns.name: datminmxid
columns.description: All multixact IDs before this one have been replaced with a transaction ID in this database. This is used to track whether the database needs to be vacuumed in order to prevent multixact ID wraparound or to allow pg_multixact to be shrunk. It is the minimum of the per-table pg_class.relminmxid values.

columns.description: The default tablespace for the database. Within this database, all tables for which pg_class.reltablespace is zero will be stored in this tablespace; in particular, all the non-shared system catalogs will be there.

columns.name: datacl
columns.description: Access privileges; see and for details

10.description: The view pg_file_settings provides a summary of the contents of the server's configuration file(s). columns.name: seqno
columns.description: Order in which the entries are processed (1..n)

columns.name: name
columns.description: Configuration parameter name

columns.name: setting
columns.description: Value to be assigned to the parameter

columns.name: applied
columns.description: True if the value can be applied successfully

columns.name: error
columns.description: If not null, an error message indicating why this entry could not be applied

10.description: The catalog pg_foreign_data_wrapper stores foreign-data wrapper definitions. A foreign-data wrapper is the mechanism by which external data, residing on foreign servers, is accessed.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: fdwname
columns.description: Name of the foreign-data wrapper

columns.name: fdwowner
columns.description: Owner of the foreign-data wrapper

columns.name: fdwhandler
columns.description: References a handler function that is responsible for supplying execution routines for the foreign-data wrapper. Zero if no handler is provided

columns.name: fdwvalidator
columns.description: References a validator function that is responsible for checking the validity of the options given to the foreign-data wrapper, as well as options for foreign servers and user mappings using the foreign-data wrapper. Zero if no validator is provided

columns.name: fdwacl
columns.description: Access privileges; see and for details

columns.name: fdwoptions
columns.description: Foreign-data wrapper specific options, as keyword=value strings

10.description: The catalog pg_index contains part of the information about indexes. The rest is mostly in pg_class.

columns.name: indexrelid
columns.description: The OID of the pg_class entry for this index

columns.name: indrelid
columns.description: The OID of the pg_class entry for the table this index is for

columns.name: indnatts
columns.description: The number of columns in the index (duplicates pg_class.relnatts)

columns.name: indisunique
columns.description: If true, this is a unique index

columns.name: indisprimary
columns.description: If true, this index represents the primary key of the table (indisunique should always be true when this is true)

columns.name: indisexclusion
columns.description: If true, this index supports an exclusion constraint

columns.name: indimmediate
columns.description: If true, the uniqueness check is enforced immediately on insertion (irrelevant if indisunique is not true)

columns.name: indisclustered
columns.description: If true, the table was last clustered on this index

columns.name: indisvalid
columns.description: If true, the index is currently valid for queries. False means the index is possibly incomplete: it must still be modified by INSERT/UPDATE operations, but it cannot safely be used for queries. If it is unique, the uniqueness property is not guaranteed true either.

columns.name: indcheckxmin
columns.description: If true, queries must not use the index until the xmin of this pg_index row is below their TransactionXmin event horizon, because the table may contain broken HOT chains with incompatible rows that they can see

columns.name: indisready
columns.description: If true, the index is currently ready for inserts. False means the index must be ignored by INSERT/UPDATE operations.

columns.name: indislive
columns.description: If false, the index is in process of being dropped, and should be ignored for all purposes (including HOT-safety decisions)

columns.name: indisreplident
columns.description: If true this index has been chosen as replica identity using ALTER TABLE ... REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX ...

columns.name: indkey
columns.description: This is an array of indnatts values that indicate which table columns this index indexes. For example a value of 1 3 would mean that the first and the third table columns make up the index key. A zero in this array indicates that the corresponding index attribute is an expression over the table columns, rather than a simple column reference.

columns.name: indcollation
columns.description: For each column in the index key, this contains the OID of the collation to use for the index, or zero if the column is not of a collatable data type.

columns.name: indclass
columns.description: For each column in the index key, this contains the OID of the operator class to use. See pg_opclass for details.

columns.name: indoption
columns.description: This is an array of indnatts values that store per-column flag bits. The meaning of the bits is defined by the index's access method.

columns.name: indexprs
columns.description: Expression trees (in nodeToString() representation) for index attributes that are not simple column references. This is a list with one element for each zero entry in indkey. Null if all index attributes are simple references.

columns.name: indpred
columns.description: Expression tree (in nodeToString() representation) for partial index predicate. Null if not a partial index.

columns.description: If true this index has been chosen as replica identity using ALTER TABLE ... REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX ...

columns.name: indkey
columns.description: This is an array of indnatts values that indicate which table columns this index indexes. For example a value of 1 3 would mean that the first and the third table columns make up the index key. A zero in this array indicates that the corresponding index attribute is an expression over the table columns, rather than a simple column reference.

columns.name: indcollation
columns.description: For each column in the index key, this contains the OID of the collation to use for the index.

columns.name: indclass
columns.description: For each column in the index key, this contains the OID of the operator class to use. See pg_opclass for details.

columns.name: indoption
columns.description: This is an array of indnatts values that store per-column flag bits. The meaning of the bits is defined by the index's access method.

columns.name: indexprs
columns.description: Expression trees (in nodeToString() representation) for index attributes that are not simple column references. This is a list with one element for each zero entry in indkey. Null if all index attributes are simple references.

columns.name: indpred
columns.description: Expression tree (in nodeToString() representation) for partial index predicate. Null if not a partial index.

19b.description: The catalog pg_index contains part of the information about indexes. The rest is mostly in pg_class.

columns.name: indexrelid
columns.description: The OID of the pg_class entry for this index

columns.name: indrelid
columns.description: The OID of the pg_class entry for the table this index is for

columns.name: indnatts
columns.description: The total number of columns in the index (duplicates pg_class.relnatts); this number includes both key and included attributes

columns.name: indnkeyatts
columns.description: The number of key columns in the index, not counting any included columns, which are merely stored and do not participate in the index semantics

columns.name: indisunique
columns.description: If true, this is a unique index

columns.name: indnullsnotdistinct
columns.description: This value is only used for unique indexes. If false, this unique index will consider null values distinct (so the index can contain multiple null values in a column, the default PostgreSQL behavior). If it is true, it will consider null values to be equal (so the index can only contain one null value in a column).

columns.name: indisprimary
columns.description: If true, this index represents the primary key of the table (indisunique should always be true when this is true)

columns.name: indisexclusion
columns.description: If true, this index supports an exclusion constraint

columns.name: indimmediate
columns.description: If true, the uniqueness check is enforced immediately on insertion (irrelevant if indisunique is not true)

columns.name: indisclustered
columns.description: If true, the table was last clustered on this index

columns.name: indisvalid
columns.description: If true, the index is currently valid for queries. False means the index is possibly incomplete: it must still be modified by INSERT/UPDATE operations, but it cannot safely be used for queries. If it is unique, the uniqueness property is not guaranteed true either.

columns.name: indcheckxmin
columns.description: If true, queries must not use the index until the xmin of this pg_index row is below their TransactionXmin event horizon, because the table may contain broken HOT chains with incompatible rows that they can see

columns.name: indisready
columns.description: If true, the index is currently ready for inserts. False means the index must be ignored by INSERT/UPDATE operations.

columns.name: indislive
columns.description: If false, the index is in process of being dropped, and should be ignored for all purposes (including HOT-safety decisions)

columns.name: indisreplident
columns.description: If true this index has been chosen as replica identity using ALTER TABLE ... REPLICA IDENTITY USING INDEX ...

columns.name: indkey
columns.description: This is an array of indnatts values that indicate which table columns this index indexes. For example, a value of 1 3 would mean that the first and the third table columns make up the index entries. Key columns come before non-key (included) columns. A zero in this array indicates that the corresponding index attribute is an expression over the table columns, rather than a simple column reference.

columns.name: indcollation
columns.description: For each column in the index key (indnkeyatts values), this contains the OID of the collation to use for the index, or zero if the column is not of a collatable data type.

columns.name: indclass
columns.description: For each column in the index key (indnkeyatts values), this contains the OID of the operator class to use. See pg_opclass for details.

columns.name: indoption
columns.description: This is an array of indnkeyatts values that store per-column flag bits. The meaning of the bits is defined by the index's access method.

columns.name: indexprs
columns.description: Expression trees (in nodeToString() representation) for index attributes that are not simple column references. This is a list with one element for each zero entry in indkey. Null if all index attributes are simple references.

columns.name: indpred
columns.description: Expression tree (in nodeToString() representation) for partial index predicate. Null if not a partial index.

10.description: The catalog pg_inherits records information about table inheritance hierarchies. There is one entry for each direct child table in the database. (Indirect inheritance can be determined by following chains of entries.)

columns.name: inhrelid
columns.description: The OID of the child table

columns.name: inhparent
columns.description: The OID of the parent table

columns.name: inhseqno
columns.description: If there is more than one direct parent for a child table (multiple inheritance), this number tells the order in which the inherited columns are to be arranged. The count starts at 1.

10.description: The catalog pg_language registers languages in which you can write functions or stored procedures. See and for more information about language handlers.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: lanname
columns.description: Name of the language

columns.name: lanowner
columns.description: Owner of the language

columns.name: lanispl
columns.description: This is false for internal languages (such as SQL) and true for user-defined languages. Currently, pg_dump still uses this to determine which languages need to be dumped, but this might be replaced by a different mechanism in the future.

columns.name: lanpltrusted
columns.description: True if this is a trusted language, which means that it is believed not to grant access to anything outside the normal SQL execution environment. Only superusers can create functions in untrusted languages.

columns.name: lanplcallfoid
columns.description: For noninternal languages this references the language handler, which is a special function that is responsible for executing all functions that are written in the particular language

columns.name: laninline
columns.description: This references a function that is responsible for executing inline anonymous code blocks ( blocks). Zero if inline blocks are not supported.

columns.name: lanvalidator
columns.description: This references a language validator function that is responsible for checking the syntax and validity of new functions when they are created. Zero if no validator is provided.

columns.name: lanacl
columns.description: Access privileges; see and for details

10.description: The catalog pg_largeobject holds the data making up large objects. A large object is identified by an OID assigned when it is created. Each large object is broken into segments or pages small enough to be conveniently stored as rows in pg_largeobject. The amount of data per page is defined to be LOBLKSIZE (which is currently BLCKSZ/4, or typically 2 kB).

columns.name: loid
columns.description: Identifier of the large object that includes this page

columns.name: pageno
columns.description: Page number of this page within its large object (counting from zero)

columns.name: data
columns.description: Actual data stored in the large object. This will never be more than LOBLKSIZE bytes and might be less.

10.description: The view pg_locks provides access to information about the locks held by active processes within the database server. See for more discussion of locking.

columns.name: locktype
columns.description: Type of the lockable object: relation, extend, frozenid, page, tuple, transactionid, virtualxid, object, userlock, or advisory

columns.name: database
columns.description: OID of the database in which the lock target exists, or zero if the target is a shared object, or null if the target is a transaction ID

columns.name: relation
columns.description: OID of the relation targeted by the lock, or null if the target is not a relation or part of a relation

columns.name: page
columns.description: Page number targeted by the lock within the relation, or null if the target is not a relation page or tuple

columns.name: tuple
columns.description: Tuple number targeted by the lock within the page, or null if the target is not a tuple

columns.name: virtualxid
columns.description: Virtual ID of the transaction targeted by the lock, or null if the target is not a virtual transaction ID

columns.name: transactionid
columns.description: ID of the transaction targeted by the lock, or null if the target is not a transaction ID

columns.name: classid
columns.description: OID of the system catalog containing the lock target, or null if the target is not a general database object

columns.name: objid
columns.description: OID of the lock target within its system catalog, or null if the target is not a general database object

columns.name: objsubid
columns.description: Column number targeted by the lock (the classid and objid refer to the table itself), or zero if the target is some other general database object, or null if the target is not a general database object

columns.name: virtualtransaction
columns.description: Virtual ID of the transaction that is holding or awaiting this lock

columns.name: pid
columns.description: Process ID of the server process holding or awaiting this lock, or null if the lock is held by a prepared transaction

columns.name: mode
columns.description: Name of the lock mode held or desired by this process (see and )

columns.name: granted
columns.description: True if lock is held, false if lock is awaited

columns.name: fastpath
columns.description: True if lock was taken via fast path, false if taken via main lock table

columns.name: objid

10.description: The catalog pg_opclass defines index access method operator classes. Each operator class defines semantics for index columns of a particular data type and a particular index access method. An operator class essentially specifies that a particular operator family is applicable to a particular indexable column data type. The set of operators from the family that are actually usable with the indexed column are whichever ones accept the column's data type as their left-hand input.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: opcmethod
columns.description: Index access method operator class is for

columns.name: opcname
columns.description: Name of this operator class

columns.name: opcnamespace
columns.description: Namespace of this operator class

columns.name: opcowner
columns.description: Owner of the operator class

columns.name: opcfamily
columns.description: Operator family containing the operator class

columns.name: opcintype
columns.description: Data type that the operator class indexes

columns.name: opcdefault

10.description: The catalog pg_opfamily defines operator families. Each operator family is a collection of operators and associated support routines that implement the semantics specified for a particular index access method. Furthermore, the operators in a family are all compatible, in a way that is specified by the access method. The operator family concept allows cross-data-type operators to be used with indexes and to be reasoned about using knowledge of access method semantics.

10.description: The catalog pg_partitioned_table stores information about how tables are partitioned.

columns.name: partrelid
columns.description: The OID of the pg_class entry for this partitioned table

columns.name: partstrat
columns.description: Partitioning strategy; l = list partitioned table, r = range partitioned table

columns.name: partnatts
columns.description: The number of columns in partition key

columns.name: partattrs
columns.description: This is an array of partnatts values that indicate which table columns are part of the partition key. For example, a value of 1 3 would mean that the first and the third table columns make up the partition key. A zero in this array indicates that the corresponding partition key column is an expression, rather than a simple column reference.

columns.name: partclass
columns.description: For each column in the partition key, this contains the OID of the operator class to use. See pg_opclass for details.

columns.name: partcollation
columns.description: For each column in the partition key, this contains the OID of the collation to use for partitioning, or zero if the column is not of a collatable data type.

columns.name: partexprs
columns.description: Expression trees (in nodeToString() representation) for partition key columns that are not simple column references. This is a list with one element for each zero entry in partattrs. Null if all partition key columns are simple references.

10.description: The catalog pg_proc stores information about functions (or procedures). See and for more information.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: proname
columns.description: Name of the function

columns.name: pronamespace
columns.description: The OID of the namespace that contains this function

columns.name: proowner
columns.description: Owner of the function

columns.name: prolang
columns.description: Implementation language or call interface of this function

columns.name: procost
columns.description: Estimated execution cost (in units of ); if proretset, this is cost per row returned

columns.name: prorows
columns.description: Estimated number of result rows (zero if not proretset)

columns.name: provariadic
columns.description: Data type of the variadic array parameter's elements, or zero if the function does not have a variadic parameter

columns.name: protransform
columns.description: Calls to this function can be simplified by this other function (see )

columns.name: proisagg
columns.description: Function is an aggregate function

columns.name: proiswindow
columns.description: Function is a window function

columns.name: prosecdef
columns.description: Function is a security definer (i.e., a setuid function)

columns.name: proleakproof
columns.description: The function has no side effects. No information about the arguments is conveyed except via the return value. Any function that might throw an error depending on the values of its arguments is not leak-proof.

columns.name: proisstrict
columns.description: Function returns null if any call argument is null. In that case the function won't actually be called at all. Functions that are not strict must be prepared to handle null inputs.

columns.name: proretset
columns.description: Function returns a set (i.e., multiple values of the specified data type)

columns.name: provolatile
columns.description: provolatile tells whether the function's result depends only on its input arguments, or is affected by outside factors. It is i for immutable functions, which always deliver the same result for the same inputs. It is s for stable functions, whose results (for fixed inputs) do not change within a scan. It is v for volatile functions, whose results might change at any time. (Use v also for functions with side-effects, so that calls to them cannot get optimized away.)

columns.name: proparallel
columns.description: proparallel tells whether the function can be safely run in parallel mode. It is s for functions which are safe to run in parallel mode without restriction. It is r for functions which can be run in parallel mode, but their execution is restricted to the parallel group leader; parallel worker processes cannot invoke these functions. It is u for functions which are unsafe in parallel mode; the presence of such a function forces a serial execution plan.

columns.name: pronargs
columns.description: Number of input arguments

columns.name: pronargdefaults
columns.description: Number of arguments that have defaults

columns.name: prorettype
columns.description: Data type of the return value

columns.name: proargtypes
columns.description: An array with the data types of the function arguments. This includes only input arguments (including INOUT and VARIADIC arguments), and thus represents the call signature of the function.

columns.name: proallargtypes
columns.description: An array with the data types of the function arguments. This includes all arguments (including OUT and INOUT arguments); however, if all the arguments are IN arguments, this field will be null. Note that subscripting is 1-based, whereas for historical reasons proargtypes is subscripted from 0.

columns.name: proargmodes
columns.description: An array with the modes of the function arguments, encoded as i for IN arguments, o for OUT arguments, b for INOUT arguments, v for VARIADIC arguments, t for TABLE arguments. If all the arguments are IN arguments, this field will be null. Note that subscripts correspond to positions of proallargtypes not proargtypes.

columns.name: proargnames
columns.description: An array with the names of the function arguments. Arguments without a name are set to empty strings in the array. If none of the arguments have a name, this field will be null. Note that subscripts correspond to positions of proallargtypes not proargtypes.

columns.name: proargdefaults
columns.description: Expression trees (in nodeToString() representation) for default values. This is a list with pronargdefaults elements, corresponding to the last N input arguments (i.e., the last N proargtypes positions). If none of the arguments have defaults, this field will be null.

columns.name: protrftypes
columns.description: Data type OIDs for which to apply transforms.

columns.name: prosrc
columns.description: This tells the function handler how to invoke the function. It might be the actual source code of the function for interpreted languages, a link symbol, a file name, or just about anything else, depending on the implementation language/call convention.

columns.name: probin
columns.description: Additional information about how to invoke the function. Again, the interpretation is language-specific.

columns.name: proconfig
columns.description: Function's local settings for run-time configuration variables

columns.name: proacl
columns.description: Access privileges; see and for details

19b.description: The catalog pg_propgraph_element stores information about the vertices and edges of a property graph, collectively called the elements of the property graph.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier

columns.name: pgepgid
columns.description: Reference to the property graph that this element belongs to

columns.name: pgerelid
columns.description: Reference to the table that contains the data for this property graph element

columns.name: pgealias
columns.description: The alias of the element. This is a unique identifier for the element within the graph. It is set when the property graph is defined and defaults to the name of the underlying element table.

columns.name: pgekind
columns.description: v for a vertex, e for an edge

columns.name: pgesrcvertexid
columns.description: For an edge, a link to the source vertex. (Zero for a vertex.)

columns.name: pgedestvertexid
columns.description: For an edge, a link to the destination vertex. (Zero for a vertex.)

columns.name: pgekey
columns.description: An array of column numbers in the table referenced by pgerelid that defines the key to use for this element table. (This defaults to the primary key when the property graph is created.)

columns.name: pgesrckey
columns.description: For an edge, an array of column numbers in the table referenced by pgerelid that defines the source key to use for this element table. (Null for a vertex.) The combination of pgesrckey and pgesrcref creates the link between the edge and the source vertex.

columns.name: pgesrcref
columns.description: For an edge, an array of column numbers in the table reached via pgesrcvertexid. (Null for a vertex.) The combination of pgesrckey and pgesrcref creates the link between the edge and the source vertex.

columns.name: pgesrceqop
columns.description: For an edge, an array of equality operators for pgesrcref = pgesrckey comparison. (Null for a vertex.)

columns.name: pgedestkey
columns.description: For an edge, an array of column numbers in the table referenced by pgerelid that defines the destination key to use for this element table. (Null for a vertex.) The combination of pgedestkey and pgedestref creates the link between the edge and the destination vertex.

columns.name: pgedestref
columns.description: For an edge, an array of column numbers in the table reached via pgedestvertexid. (Null for a vertex.) The combination of pgedestkey and pgedestref creates the link between the edge and the destination vertex.

columns.name: pgedesteqop
columns.description: For an edge, an array of equality operators for pgedestref = pgedestkey comparison. (Null for a vertex.)

10.description: The pg_replication_slots view provides a listing of all replication slots that currently exist on the database cluster, along with their current state.

columns.name: slot_name
columns.description: A unique, cluster-wide identifier for the replication slot

columns.name: plugin
columns.description: The base name of the shared object containing the output plugin this logical slot is using, or null for physical slots.

columns.name: slot_type
columns.description: The slot type - physical or logical

columns.name: datoid
columns.description: The OID of the database this slot is associated with, or null. Only logical slots have an associated database.

columns.name: database
columns.description: The name of the database this slot is associated with, or null. Only logical slots have an associated database.

columns.name: temporary
columns.description: True if this is a temporary replication slot. Temporary slots are not saved to disk and are automatically dropped on error or when the session has finished.

columns.name: active
columns.description: True if this slot is currently actively being used

columns.name: active_pid
columns.description: The process ID of the session using this slot if the slot is currently actively being used. NULL if inactive.

columns.name: xmin
columns.description: The oldest transaction that this slot needs the database to retain. VACUUM cannot remove tuples deleted by any later transaction.

columns.name: catalog_xmin
columns.description: The oldest transaction affecting the system catalogs that this slot needs the database to retain. VACUUM cannot remove catalog tuples deleted by any later transaction.

columns.name: restart_lsn
columns.description: The address (LSN) of oldest WAL which still might be required by the consumer of this slot and thus won't be automatically removed during checkpoints.

columns.name: confirmed_flush_lsn
columns.description: The address (LSN) up to which the logical slot's consumer has confirmed receiving data. Data older than this is not available anymore. NULL for physical slots.

columns.description: The base name of the shared object containing the output plugin this logical slot is using, or null for physical slots.

columns.name: slot_type
columns.description: The slot type: physical or logical

columns.name: datoid
columns.description: The OID of the database this slot is associated with, or null. Only logical slots have an associated database.

columns.name: database
columns.description: The name of the database this slot is associated with, or null. Only logical slots have an associated database.

columns.name: temporary
columns.description: True if this is a temporary replication slot. Temporary slots are not saved to disk and are automatically dropped on error or when the session has finished.

columns.name: active
columns.description: True if this slot is currently being streamed

columns.name: active_pid
columns.description: The process ID of the session streaming data for this slot. NULL if inactive.

columns.name: xmin
columns.description: The oldest transaction that this slot needs the database to retain. VACUUM cannot remove tuples deleted by any later transaction.

columns.name: catalog_xmin
columns.description: The oldest transaction affecting the system catalogs that this slot needs the database to retain. VACUUM cannot remove catalog tuples deleted by any later transaction.

columns.name: restart_lsn
columns.description: The address (LSN) of oldest WAL which still might be required by the consumer of this slot and thus won't be automatically removed during checkpoints unless this LSN gets behind more than from the current LSN. NULL if the LSN of this slot has never been reserved.

columns.name: confirmed_flush_lsn
columns.description: The address (LSN) up to which the logical slot's consumer has confirmed receiving data. Data corresponding to the transactions committed before this LSN is not available anymore. NULL for physical slots.

columns.name: wal_status
columns.description: Availability of WAL files claimed by this slot. Possible values are: reserved means that the claimed files are within max_wal_size.

columns.name: safe_wal_size
columns.description: The number of bytes that can be written to WAL such that this slot is not in danger of getting in state "lost". It is NULL for lost slots, as well as if max_slot_wal_keep_size is -1.

columns.name: two_phase
columns.description: True if the slot is enabled for decoding prepared transactions. Always false for physical slots.

columns.name: inactive_since
columns.description: The time when the slot became inactive. NULL if the slot is currently being streamed. Note that for slots on the standby that are being synced from a primary server (whose synced field is true), the inactive_since indicates the time when slot synchronization (see ) was most recently stopped. NULL if the slot has always been synchronized. On standby, this is useful for slots that are being synced from a primary server (whose synced field is true) so they know when the slot stopped being synchronized.

columns.name: conflicting
columns.description: True if this logical slot conflicted with recovery (and so is now invalidated). When this column is true, check invalidation_reason column for the conflict reason. Always NULL for physical slots.

columns.name: invalidation_reason
columns.description: The reason for the slot's invalidation. It is set for both logical and physical slots. NULL if the slot is not invalidated. Possible values are: wal_removed means that the required WAL has been removed.

columns.name: failover
columns.description: True if this is a logical slot enabled to be synced to the standbys so that logical replication can be resumed from the new primary after failover. Always false for physical slots.

columns.name: synced
columns.description: True if this is a logical slot that was synced from a primary server. On a hot standby, the slots with the synced column marked as true can neither be used for logical decoding nor dropped manually. The value of this column has no meaning on the primary server; the column value on the primary is default false for all slots but may (if leftover from a promoted standby) also be true.

10.description: The view pg_settings provides access to run-time parameters of the server. It is essentially an alternative interface to the and commands. It also provides access to some facts about each parameter that are not directly available from SHOW, such as minimum and maximum values.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Run-time configuration parameter name

columns.name: setting
columns.description: Current value of the parameter

columns.name: unit
columns.description: Implicit unit of the parameter

columns.name: category
columns.description: Logical group of the parameter

columns.name: short_desc
columns.description: A brief description of the parameter

columns.name: extra_desc
columns.description: Additional, more detailed, description of the parameter

columns.name: context
columns.description: Context required to set the parameter's value (see below)

columns.name: vartype
columns.description: Parameter type (bool, enum, integer, real, or string)

columns.name: source
columns.description: Source of the current parameter value

columns.name: min_val
columns.description: Minimum allowed value of the parameter (null for non-numeric values)

columns.name: max_val
columns.description: Maximum allowed value of the parameter (null for non-numeric values)

columns.name: enumvals
columns.description: Allowed values of an enum parameter (null for non-enum values)

columns.name: boot_val
columns.description: Parameter value assumed at server startup if the parameter is not otherwise set

columns.name: reset_val
columns.description: Value that RESET would reset the parameter to in the current session

columns.name: sourcefile
columns.description: Configuration file the current value was set in (null for values set from sources other than configuration files, or when examined by a user who is neither a superuser or a member of pg_read_all_settings); helpful when using include directives in configuration files

columns.name: sourceline
columns.description: Line number within the configuration file the current value was set at (null for values set from sources other than configuration files, or when examined by a user who is neither a superuser or a member of pg_read_all_settings).

columns.name: pending_restart
columns.description: true if the value has been changed in the configuration file but needs a restart; or false otherwise.

10.description: The catalog pg_shdepend records the dependency relationships between database objects and shared objects, such as roles. This information allows PostgreSQL to ensure that those objects are unreferenced before attempting to delete them.

columns.name: dbid
columns.description: The OID of the database the dependent object is in, or zero for a shared object

columns.name: classid
columns.description: The OID of the system catalog the dependent object is in

columns.name: objid
columns.description: The OID of the specific dependent object

columns.name: objsubid
columns.description: For a table column, this is the column number (the objid and classid refer to the table itself). For all other object types, this column is zero.

columns.name: refclassid
columns.description: The OID of the system catalog the referenced object is in (must be a shared catalog)

columns.name: refobjid
columns.description: The OID of the specific referenced object

columns.name: deptype
columns.description: A code defining the specific semantics of this dependency relationship; see text

13.description: The pg_shmem_allocations view shows allocations made from the server's main shared memory segment. This includes both memory allocated by postgres itself and memory allocated by extensions using the mechanisms detailed in .

columns.name: name
columns.description: The name of the shared memory allocation. NULL for unused memory and <anonymous> for anonymous allocations.

columns.name: off
columns.description: The offset at which the allocation starts. NULL for anonymous allocations, since details related to them are not known.

columns.name: size
columns.description: Size of the allocation

columns.name: allocated_size
columns.description: Size of the allocation including padding. For anonymous allocations, no information about padding is available, so the size and allocated_size columns will always be equal. Padding is not meaningful for free memory, so the columns will be equal in that case also.

18.description: The pg_shmem_allocations_numa shows how shared memory allocations in the server's main shared memory segment are distributed across NUMA nodes. This includes both memory allocated by PostgreSQL itself and memory allocated by extensions using the mechanisms detailed in . This view will output multiple rows for each of the shared memory segments provided that they are spread across multiple NUMA nodes. This view should not be queried by monitoring systems as it is very slow and may end up allocating shared memory in case it was not used earlier. Current limitation for this view is that won't show anonymous shared memory allocations.

10.description: The pg_statio_ views are primarily useful to determine the effectiveness of the buffer cache. When the number of actual disk reads is much smaller than the number of buffer hits, then the cache is satisfying most read requests without invoking a kernel call. However, these statistics do not give the entire story: due to the way in which PostgreSQL handles disk I/O, data that is not in the PostgreSQL buffer cache might still reside in the kernel's I/O cache, and might therefore still be fetched without requiring a physical read. Users interested in obtaining more detailed information on PostgreSQL I/O behavior are advised to use the PostgreSQL statistics collector in combination with operating system utilities that allow insight into the kernel's handling of I/O.

columns.name: datid
columns.description: OID of the database this backend is connected to

columns.name: datname
columns.description: Name of the database this backend is connected to

columns.name: pid
columns.description: Process ID of this backend

columns.name: usesysid
columns.description: OID of the user logged into this backend

columns.name: usename
columns.description: Name of the user logged into this backend

columns.name: application_name
columns.description: Name of the application that is connected to this backend

columns.name: client_addr
columns.description: IP address of the client connected to this backend. If this field is null, it indicates either that the client is connected via a Unix socket on the server machine or that this is an internal process such as autovacuum.

columns.name: client_hostname
columns.description: Host name of the connected client, as reported by a reverse DNS lookup of client_addr. This field will only be non-null for IP connections, and only when is enabled.

columns.name: client_port
columns.description: TCP port number that the client is using for communication with this backend, or -1 if a Unix socket is used

columns.name: backend_start
columns.description: Time when this process was started. For client backends, this is the time the client connected to the server.

columns.name: xact_start
columns.description: Time when this process' current transaction was started, or null if no transaction is active. If the current query is the first of its transaction, this column is equal to the query_start column.

columns.name: query_start
columns.description: Time when the currently active query was started, or if state is not active, when the last query was started

columns.name: state_change
columns.description: Time when the state was last changed

columns.name: wait_event_type
columns.description: The type of event for which the backend is waiting, if any; otherwise NULL. Possible values are: LWLock: The backend is waiting for a lightweight lock. Each such lock protects a particular data structure in shared memory. wait_event will contain a name identifying the purpose of the lightweight lock. (Some locks have specific names; others are part of a group of locks each with a similar purpose.) Lock: The backend is waiting for a heavyweight lock. Heavyweight locks, also known as lock manager locks or simply locks, primarily protect SQL-visible objects such as tables. However, they are also used to ensure mutual exclusion for certain internal operations such as relation extension. wait_event will identify the type of lock awaited. BufferPin: The server process is waiting to access to a data buffer during a period when no other process can be examining that buffer. Buffer pin waits can be protracted if another process holds an open cursor which last read data from the buffer in question. Activity: The server process is idle. This is used by system processes waiting for activity in their main processing loop. wait_event will identify the specific wait point. Extension: The server process is waiting for activity in an extension module. This category is useful for modules to track custom waiting points. Client: The server process is waiting for some activity on a socket from user applications, and that the server expects something to happen that is independent from its internal processes. wait_event will identify the specific wait point. IPC: The server process is waiting for some activity from another process in the server. wait_event will identify the specific wait point. Timeout: The server process is waiting for a timeout to expire. wait_event will identify the specific wait point. IO: The server process is waiting for a IO to complete. wait_event will identify the specific wait point.

columns.name: wait_event
columns.description: Wait event name if backend is currently waiting, otherwise NULL. See for details.

columns.name: state
columns.description: Current overall state of this backend. Possible values are: active: The backend is executing a query. idle: The backend is waiting for a new client command. idle in transaction: The backend is in a transaction, but is not currently executing a query. idle in transaction (aborted): This state is similar to idle in transaction, except one of the statements in the transaction caused an error. fastpath function call: The backend is executing a fast-path function. disabled: This state is reported if is disabled in this backend.

columns.name: backend_xid
columns.description: Top-level transaction identifier of this backend, if any.

columns.name: backend_xmin
columns.description: The current backend's xmin horizon.

columns.name: query
columns.description: Text of this backend's most recent query. If state is active this field shows the currently executing query. In all other states, it shows the last query that was executed. By default the query text is truncated at 1024 bytes; this value can be changed via the parameter .

columns.name: backend_type
columns.description: Type of current backend. Possible types are autovacuum launcher, autovacuum worker, background worker, background writer, client backend, checkpointer, startup, walreceiver, walsender and walwriter.

12.description: The pg_statio_ views are primarily useful to determine the effectiveness of the buffer cache. When the number of actual disk reads is much smaller than the number of buffer hits, then the cache is satisfying most read requests without invoking a kernel call. columns.description: The type of event for which the backend is waiting, if any; otherwise NULL. Possible values are: LWLockNamed: The backend is waiting for a specific named lightweight lock. Each such lock protects a particular data structure in shared memory. wait_event will contain the name of the lightweight lock. LWLockTranche: The backend is waiting for one of a group of related lightweight locks. All locks in the group perform a similar function; wait_event will identify the general purpose of locks in that group. Lock: The backend is waiting for a heavyweight lock. Heavyweight locks, also known as lock manager locks or simply locks, primarily protect SQL-visible objects such as tables. However, they are also used to ensure mutual exclusion for certain internal operations such as relation extension. wait_event will identify the type of lock awaited. BufferPin: The server process is waiting to access to a data buffer during a period when no other process can be examining that buffer. Buffer pin waits can be protracted if another process holds an open cursor which last read data from the buffer in question.

columns.name: wait_event
columns.description: Wait event name if backend is currently waiting, otherwise NULL. See for details.

columns.name: state
columns.description: Current overall state of this backend. Possible values are: active: The backend is executing a query. idle: The backend is waiting for a new client command. idle in transaction: The backend is in a transaction, but is not currently executing a query. idle in transaction (aborted): This state is similar to idle in transaction, except one of the statements in the transaction caused an error. fastpath function call: The backend is executing a fast-path function. disabled: This state is reported if is disabled in this backend.

columns.name: backend_xid
columns.description: Top-level transaction identifier of this backend, if any.

columns.name: backend_xmin
columns.description: The current backend's xmin horizon.

columns.name: query
columns.description: Text of this backend's most recent query. If state is active this field shows the currently executing query. In all other states, it shows the last query that was executed.

19b.description: The pg_stat_autovacuum_scores view will contain one row for each table in the current database (including TOAST tables), showing the current autovacuum scores for that specific table. Autovacuum prioritizes tables deemed eligible for processing based on their score, with higher scores indicating higher priority. See for more information.

columns.name: relid
columns.description: Oid of the table.

columns.name: schemaname
columns.description: Name of the schema that the table is in.

columns.name: relname
columns.description: Name of the table.

columns.name: score
columns.description: Maximum value of all component scores. This is the value that autovacuum would use to sort the list of tables to process.

columns.name: xid_score
columns.description: Transaction ID age component score. Scores greater than indicate that autovacuum would vacuum the table for transaction ID wraparound prevention.

columns.name: mxid_score
columns.description: Multixact ID age component score. Scores greater than indicate that autovacuum would vacuum the table for multixact ID wraparound prevention.

columns.name: vacuum_score
columns.description: Vacuum component score. Scores greater than indicate that autovacuum would vacuum the table (unless autovacuum is disabled).

columns.name: vacuum_insert_score
columns.description: Vacuum insert component score. Scores greater than indicate that autovacuum would vacuum the table (unless autovacuum is disabled).

16.description: The pg_stat_io view will contain one row for each combination of backend type, target I/O object, and I/O context, showing cluster-wide I/O statistics. Combinations which do not make sense are omitted.

columns.name: backend_type
columns.description: Type of backend (e.g. background worker, autovacuum worker). See pg_stat_activity for more information on backend_types. Some backend_types do not accumulate I/O operation statistics and will not be included in the view.

columns.name: object
columns.description: Target object of an I/O operation. Possible values are: relation: Permanent relations.

columns.name: context
columns.description: The context of an I/O operation. Possible values are:

columns.name: reads
columns.description: Number of read operations, each of the size specified in op_bytes.

columns.name: read_time
columns.description: Time spent in read operations in milliseconds (if is enabled, otherwise zero)

columns.name: writes
columns.description: Number of write operations, each of the size specified in op_bytes.

columns.name: write_time
columns.description: Time spent in write operations in milliseconds (if is enabled, otherwise zero)

columns.name: writebacks
columns.description: Number of units of size op_bytes which the process requested the kernel write out to permanent storage.

columns.name: writeback_time
columns.description: Time spent in writeback operations in milliseconds (if is enabled, otherwise zero). This includes the time spent queueing write-out requests and, potentially, the time spent to write out the dirty data.

columns.name: extends
columns.description: Number of relation extend operations, each of the size specified in op_bytes.

columns.name: extend_time
columns.description: Time spent in extend operations in milliseconds (if is enabled, otherwise zero)

columns.name: op_bytes
columns.description: The number of bytes per unit of I/O read, written, or extended.

columns.name: hits
columns.description: The number of times a desired block was found in a shared buffer.

columns.name: evictions
columns.description: Number of times a block has been written out from a shared or local buffer in order to make it available for another use.

columns.name: reuses
columns.description: The number of times an existing buffer in a size-limited ring buffer outside of shared buffers was reused as part of an I/O operation in the bulkread, bulkwrite, or vacuum contexts.

columns.name: fsyncs
columns.description: Number of fsync calls. These are only tracked in context normal.

columns.name: fsync_time
columns.description: Time spent in fsync operations in milliseconds (if is enabled, otherwise zero)

columns.name: stats_reset
columns.description: Time at which these statistics were last reset.

When enabling data checksums, the view will also contain one row for each worker process which is currently calculating and writing checksums for the data pages in a database. The launcher provides an overview of the overall progress, such as how many databases have been processed and how many remain, while the workers track progress for currently processed databases.
