columns.name: pid
columns.description: Process ID of a WAL sender process

columns.name: usesysid
columns.description: OID of the user logged into this WAL sender process

columns.name: usename
columns.description: Name of the user logged into this WAL sender process

columns.name: application_name
columns.description: Name of the application that is connected to this WAL sender

columns.name: client_addr
columns.description: IP address of the client connected to this WAL sender. If this field is null, it indicates that the client is connected via a Unix socket on the server machine.

columns.name: client_hostname
columns.description: Host name of the connected client, as reported by a reverse DNS lookup of client_addr. This field will only be non-null for IP connections, and only when is enabled.

columns.name: client_port
columns.description: TCP port number that the client is using for communication with this WAL sender, or -1 if a Unix socket is used

columns.name: backend_start
columns.description: Time when this process was started, i.e., when the client connected to this WAL sender

columns.name: backend_xmin
columns.description: This standby's xmin horizon reported by .

columns.name: state
columns.description: Current WAL sender state. Possible values are: startup: This WAL sender is starting up. catchup: This WAL sender's connected standby is catching up with the primary. streaming: This WAL sender is streaming changes after its connected standby server has caught up with the primary. backup: This WAL sender is sending a backup. stopping: This WAL sender is stopping.

columns.name: sent_lsn
columns.description: Last write-ahead log location sent on this connection

columns.name: write_lsn
columns.description: Last write-ahead log location written to disk by this standby server

columns.name: flush_lsn
columns.description: Last write-ahead log location flushed to disk by this standby server

columns.name: replay_lsn
columns.description: Last write-ahead log location replayed into the database on this standby server

columns.name: write_lag
columns.description: Time elapsed between flushing recent WAL locally and receiving notification that this standby server has written it (but not yet flushed it or applied it). This can be used to gauge the delay that synchronous_commit level remote_write incurred while committing if this server was configured as a synchronous standby.

columns.name: flush_lag
columns.description: Time elapsed between flushing recent WAL locally and receiving notification that this standby server has written and flushed it (but not yet applied it). This can be used to gauge the delay that synchronous_commit level on incurred while committing if this server was configured as a synchronous standby.

columns.name: replay_lag
columns.description: Time elapsed between flushing recent WAL locally and receiving notification that this standby server has written, flushed and applied it. This can be used to gauge the delay that synchronous_commit level remote_apply incurred while committing if this server was configured as a synchronous standby.

columns.name: sync_priority
columns.description: Priority of this standby server for being chosen as the synchronous standby in a priority-based synchronous replication. This has no effect in a quorum-based synchronous replication.

columns.name: sync_state
columns.description: Synchronous state of this standby server. Possible values are: async: This standby server is asynchronous. potential: This standby server is now asynchronous, but can potentially become synchronous if one of current synchronous ones fails. sync: This standby server is synchronous. quorum: This standby server is considered as a candidate for quorum standbys.

14.description: The pg_stat_replication_slots view will contain one row per logical replication slot, showing statistics about its usage.

columns.name: slot_name
columns.description: A unique, cluster-wide identifier for the replication slot

columns.name: spill_txns
columns.description: Number of transactions spilled to disk once the memory used by logical decoding to decode changes from WAL has exceeded logical_decoding_work_mem. The counter gets incremented for both top-level transactions and subtransactions.

columns.name: spill_count
columns.description: Number of times transactions were spilled to disk while decoding changes from WAL for this slot. This counter is incremented each time a transaction is spilled, and the same transaction may be spilled multiple times.

columns.name: spill_bytes
columns.description: Amount of decoded transaction data spilled to disk while performing decoding of changes from WAL for this slot. This and other spill counters can be used to gauge the I/O which occurred during logical decoding and allow tuning logical_decoding_work_mem.

columns.name: stream_txns
columns.description: Number of in-progress transactions streamed to the decoding output plugin after the memory used by logical decoding to decode changes from WAL for this slot has exceeded logical_decoding_work_mem. Streaming only works with top-level transactions (subtransactions can't be streamed independently), so the counter is not incremented for subtransactions.

columns.name: stream_count
columns.description: Number of times in-progress transactions were streamed to the decoding output plugin while decoding changes from WAL for this slot. This counter is incremented each time a transaction is streamed, and the same transaction may be streamed multiple times.

columns.name: stream_bytes
columns.description: Amount of transaction data decoded for streaming in-progress transactions to the decoding output plugin while decoding changes from WAL for this slot. This and other streaming counters for this slot can be used to tune logical_decoding_work_mem.

columns.name: total_txns
columns.description: Number of decoded transactions sent to the decoding output plugin for this slot. This counts top-level transactions only, and is not incremented for subtransactions. Note that this includes the transactions that are streamed and/or spilled.

columns.name: total_bytes
columns.description: Amount of transaction data decoded for sending transactions to the decoding output plugin while decoding changes from WAL for this slot. Note that this includes data that is streamed and/or spilled.

columns.name: stats_reset
columns.description: Time at which these statistics were last reset

columns.description: Number of times a row insertion or an updated row values violated multiple NOT DEFERRABLE unique constraints during the application of changes. See for details about this conflict.

10.description: The reported lag times are not predictions of how long it will take for the standby to catch up with the sending server assuming the current rate of replay. Such a system would show similar times while new WAL is being generated, but would differ when the sender becomes idle. In particular, when the standby has caught up completely, pg_stat_replication shows the time taken to write, flush and replay the most recent reported WAL location rather than zero as some users might expect. This is consistent with the goal of measuring synchronous commit and transaction visibility delays for recent write transactions. To reduce confusion for users expecting a different model of lag, the lag columns revert to NULL after a short time on a fully replayed idle system. Monitoring systems should choose whether to represent this as missing data, zero or continue to display the last known value.

10.description: The catalog pg_statistic stores statistical data about the contents of the database. Entries are created by and subsequently used by the query planner. Note that all the statistical data is inherently approximate, even assuming that it is up-to-date.

columns.name: starelid
columns.description: The table or index that the described column belongs to

columns.name: staattnum
columns.description: The number of the described column

columns.name: stainherit
columns.description: If true, the stats include inheritance child columns, not just the values in the specified relation

columns.name: stanullfrac
columns.description: The fraction of the column's entries that are null

columns.name: stawidth
columns.description: The average stored width, in bytes, of nonnull entries

columns.name: stadistinct
columns.description: The number of distinct nonnull data values in the column. A value greater than zero is the actual number of distinct values. A value less than zero is the negative of a multiplier for the number of rows in the table; for example, a column in which about 80% of the values are nonnull and each nonnull value appears about twice on average could be represented by stadistinct = -0.4. A zero value means the number of distinct values is unknown.

columns.name: stakindN
columns.description: A code number indicating the kind of statistics stored in the Nth slot of the pg_statistic row.

columns.name: staopN
columns.description: An operator used to derive the statistics stored in the Nth slot. For example, a histogram slot would show the < operator that defines the sort order of the data.

columns.name: stanumbersN
columns.description: Numerical statistics of the appropriate kind for the Nth slot, or null if the slot kind does not involve numerical values

columns.name: stavaluesN
columns.description: Column data values of the appropriate kind for the Nth slot, or null if the slot kind does not store any data values. Each array's element values are actually of the specific column's data type, or a related type such as an array's element type, so there is no way to define these columns' type more specifically than anyarray.

10.description: The view pg_stats provides access to the information stored in the pg_statistic catalog. This view allows access only to rows of pg_statistic that correspond to tables the user has permission to read, and therefore it is safe to allow public read access to this view.

columns.name: schemaname
columns.description: Name of schema containing table

columns.name: tablename
columns.description: Name of table

columns.name: attname
columns.description: Name of the column described by this row

columns.name: inherited
columns.description: If true, this row includes inheritance child columns, not just the values in the specified table

columns.name: null_frac
columns.description: Fraction of column entries that are null

columns.name: avg_width
columns.description: Average width in bytes of column's entries

columns.name: n_distinct
columns.description: If greater than zero, the estimated number of distinct values in the column. If less than zero, the negative of the number of distinct values divided by the number of rows. (The negated form is used when ANALYZE believes that the number of distinct values is likely to increase as the table grows; the positive form is used when the column seems to have a fixed number of possible values.) For example, -1 indicates a unique column in which the number of distinct values is the same as the number of rows.

columns.name: most_common_vals
columns.description: A list of the most common values in the column. (Null if no values seem to be more common than any others.)

columns.name: most_common_freqs
columns.description: A list of the frequencies of the most common values, i.e., number of occurrences of each divided by total number of rows. (Null when most_common_vals is.)

columns.name: histogram_bounds
columns.description: A list of values that divide the column's values into groups of approximately equal population. The values in most_common_vals, if present, are omitted from this histogram calculation. (This column is null if the column data type does not have a < operator or if the most_common_vals list accounts for the entire population.)

columns.name: correlation
columns.description: Statistical correlation between physical row ordering and logical ordering of the column values. This ranges from -1 to +1. When the value is near -1 or +1, an index scan on the column will be estimated to be cheaper than when it is near zero, due to reduction of random access to the disk. (This column is null if the column data type does not have a < operator.)

columns.name: most_common_elems
columns.description: A list of non-null element values most often appearing within values of the column. (Null for scalar types.)

columns.name: most_common_elem_freqs
columns.description: A list of the frequencies of the most common element values, i.e., the fraction of rows containing at least one instance of the given value. Two or three additional values follow the per-element frequencies; these are the minimum and maximum of the preceding per-element frequencies, and optionally the frequency of null elements. (Null when most_common_elems is.)

columns.name: elem_count_histogram
columns.description: A histogram of the counts of distinct non-null element values within the values of the column, followed by the average number of distinct non-null elements. (Null for scalar types.)

columns.description: Fraction of expression entries that are null

columns.description: Average width in bytes of expression's entries

columns.name: n_distinct
columns.description: If greater than zero, the estimated number of distinct values in the expression. If less than zero, the negative of the number of distinct values divided by the number of rows. (The negated form is used when ANALYZE believes that the number of distinct values is likely to increase as the table grows; the positive form is used when the expression seems to have a fixed number of possible values.) columns.name: most_common_vals
columns.description: A list of the most common values in the expression. (Null if no values seem to be more common than any others.)

columns.name: most_common_freqs
columns.description: A list of the frequencies of the most common values, i.e., number of occurrences of each divided by total number of rows. (Null when most_common_vals is.)

columns.name: histogram_bounds
columns.description: A list of values that divide the expression's values into groups of approximately equal population. The values in most_common_vals, if present, are omitted from this histogram calculation. (This expression is null if the expression data type does not have a < operator or if the most_common_vals list accounts for the entire population.)

columns.name: correlation
columns.description: Statistical correlation between physical row ordering and logical ordering of the expression values. This ranges from -1 to +1. When the value is near -1 or +1, an index scan on the expression will be estimated to be cheaper than when it is near zero, due to reduction of random access to the disk. (This expression is null if the expression's data type does not have a < operator.)

columns.name: most_common_elems
columns.description: A list of non-null element values most often appearing within values of the expression. (Null for scalar types.)

columns.name: most_common_elem_freqs
columns.description: A list of the frequencies of the most common element values, i.e., the fraction of rows containing at least one instance of the given value. Two or three additional values follow the per-element frequencies; these are the minimum and maximum of the preceding per-element frequencies, and optionally the frequency of null elements. (Null when most_common_elems is.)

columns.name: elem_count_histogram
columns.description: A histogram of the counts of distinct non-null element values within the values of the expression, followed by the average number of distinct non-null elements. (Null for scalar types.)

(This expression is null if the expression data type does not have a < operator or if the most_common_vals list accounts for the entire population.)

columns.name: correlation
columns.description: Statistical correlation between physical row ordering and logical ordering of the expression values. This ranges from -1 to +1. When the value is near -1 or +1, an index scan on the expression will be estimated to be cheaper than when it is near zero, due to reduction of random access to the disk. (This expression is null if the expression's data type does not have a < operator.)

columns.name: most_common_elems
columns.description: A list of non-null element values most often appearing within values of the expression. (Null for scalar types.)

columns.name: most_common_elem_freqs
columns.description: A list of the frequencies of the most common element values, i.e., the fraction of rows containing at least one instance of the given value. Two or three additional values follow the per-element frequencies; these are the minimum and maximum of the preceding per-element frequencies, and optionally the frequency of null elements. (Null when most_common_elems is.)

columns.name: elem_count_histogram
columns.description: A histogram of the counts of distinct non-null element values within the values of the expression, followed by the average number of distinct non-null elements. (Null for scalar types.)

columns.name: range_length_histogram
columns.description: A histogram of the lengths of non-empty and non-null range values of an expression. (Null for non-range types.)

columns.name: range_empty_frac
columns.description: Fraction of expression entries whose values are empty ranges. (Null for non-range types.)

columns.name: range_bounds_histogram
columns.description: A histogram of lower and upper bounds of non-empty and non-null range values. (Null for non-range types.)

10.description: The view pg_timezone_names provides a list of time zone names that are recognized by SET TIMEZONE, along with their associated abbreviations, UTC offsets, and daylight-savings status. (Technically, PostgreSQL does not use UTC because leap seconds are not handled.) Unlike the abbreviations shown in pg_timezone_abbrevs, many of these names imply a set of daylight-savings transition date rules. Therefore, the associated information changes across local DST boundaries. The displayed information is computed based on the current value of CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.

columns.description: True if currently observing daylight savings

columns.description: OID of the language this transform is for

A configuration specifies a particular text search parser and a list of dictionaries to use for each of the parser's output token types. The parser is shown in the pg_ts_config entry, but the token-to-dictionary mapping is defined by subsidiary entries in pg_ts_config_map.

columns.name: cfgnamespace
columns.description: The OID of the namespace that contains this configuration

columns.name: cfgowner
columns.description: Owner of the configuration

columns.name: cfgparser
columns.description: The OID of the text search parser for this configuration

10.description: The pg_ts_dict catalog contains entries defining text search dictionaries. A dictionary depends on a text search template, which specifies all the implementation functions needed; the dictionary itself provides values for the user-settable parameters supported by the template. This division of labor allows dictionaries to be created by unprivileged users. The parameters are specified by a text string dictinitoption, whose format and meaning vary depending on the template.

columns.description: The OID of the text search template for this dictionary

columns.name: dictinitoption
columns.description: Initialization option string for the template

10.description: The catalog pg_type stores information about data types. Base types and enum types (scalar types) are created with , and domains with . A composite type is automatically created for each table in the database, to represent the row structure of the table. It is also possible to create composite types with CREATE TYPE AS.

columns.name: oid
columns.description: Row identifier (hidden attribute; must be explicitly selected)

columns.name: typname
columns.description: Data type name

columns.name: typnamespace
columns.description: The OID of the namespace that contains this type

columns.name: typowner
columns.description: Owner of the type

columns.name: typlen
columns.description: For a fixed-size type, typlen is the number of bytes in the internal representation of the type. But for a variable-length type, typlen is negative. -1 indicates a varlena type (one that has a length word), -2 indicates a null-terminated C string.

columns.name: typbyval
columns.description: typbyval determines whether internal routines pass a value of this type by value or by reference. typbyval had better be false if typlen is not 1, 2, or 4 (or 8 on machines where Datum is 8 bytes). Variable-length types are always passed by reference. Note that typbyval can be false even if the length would allow pass-by-value.

columns.name: typtype
columns.description: typtype is b for a base type, c for a composite type (e.g., a table's row type), d for a domain, e for an enum type, p for a pseudo-type, or r for a range type. See also typrelid and typbasetype.

columns.name: typcategory
columns.description: typcategory is an arbitrary classification of data types that is used by the parser to determine which implicit casts should be preferred. See .

columns.name: typispreferred
columns.description: True if the type is a preferred cast target within its typcategory

columns.name: typisdefined
columns.description: True if the type is defined, false if this is a placeholder entry for a not-yet-defined type. When typisdefined is false, nothing except the type name, namespace, and OID can be relied on.

columns.name: typdelim
columns.description: Character that separates two values of this type when parsing array input. Note that the delimiter is associated with the array element data type, not the array data type.

columns.name: typrelid
columns.description: If this is a composite type (see typtype), then this column points to the pg_class entry that defines the corresponding table. (For a free-standing composite type, the pg_class entry doesn't really represent a table, but it is needed anyway for the type's pg_attribute entries to link to.) Zero for non-composite types.

columns.name: typelem
columns.description: If typelem is not 0 then it identifies another row in pg_type. The current type can then be subscripted like an array yielding values of type typelem. A true array type is variable length (typlen = -1), but some fixed-length (typlen > 0) types also have nonzero typelem, for example name and point. If a fixed-length type has a typelem then its internal representation must be some number of values of the typelem data type with no other data. Variable-length array types have a header defined by the array subroutines.

columns.name: typarray
columns.description: If typarray is not 0 then it identifies another row in pg_type, which is the true array type having this type as element

columns.name: typinput
columns.description: Input conversion function (text format)

columns.name: typoutput
columns.description: Output conversion function (text format)

columns.name: typreceive
columns.description: Input conversion function (binary format), or 0 if none

columns.name: typsend
columns.description: Output conversion function (binary format), or 0 if none

columns.name: typmodin
columns.description: Type modifier input function, or 0 if type does not support modifiers

columns.name: typmodout
columns.description: Type modifier output function, or 0 to use the standard format

columns.name: typanalyze
columns.description: Custom ANALYZE function, or 0 to use the standard function

columns.name: typalign
columns.description: typalign is the alignment required when storing a value of this type. It applies to storage on disk as well as most representations of the value inside PostgreSQL. When multiple values are stored consecutively, such as in the representation of a complete row on disk, padding is inserted before a datum of this type so that it begins on the specified boundary. The alignment reference is the beginning of the first datum in the sequence. Possible values are: c = char alignment, i.e., no alignment needed. s = short alignment (2 bytes on most machines). i = int alignment (4 bytes on most machines). d = double alignment (8 bytes on many machines, but by no means all). For types used in system tables, it is critical that the size and alignment defined in pg_type agree with the way that the compiler will lay out the column in a structure representing a table row.

columns.name: typstorage
columns.description: typstorage tells for varlena types (those with typlen = -1) if the type is prepared for toasting and what the default strategy for attributes of this type should be. Possible values are p: Value must always be stored plain. e: Value can be stored in a secondary relation (if relation has one, see pg_class.reltoastrelid). m: Value can be stored compressed inline. x: Value can be stored compressed inline or stored in secondary storage. Note that m columns can also be moved out to secondary storage, but only as a last resort (e and x columns are moved first).

columns.name: typnotnull
columns.description: typnotnull represents a not-null constraint on a type. Used for domains only.

columns.name: typbasetype
columns.description: If this is a domain (see typtype), then typbasetype identifies the type that this one is based on. Zero if this type is not a domain.

columns.name: typtypmod
columns.description: Domains use typtypmod to record the typmod to be applied to their base type (-1 if base type does not use a typmod). -1 if this type is not a domain.

columns.name: typndims
columns.description: typndims is the number of array dimensions for a domain over an array (that is, typbasetype is an array type). Zero for types other than domains over array types.

columns.name: typcollation
columns.description: typcollation specifies the collation of the type. If the type does not support collations, this will be zero. A base type that supports collations will have DEFAULT_COLLATION_OID here. A domain over a collatable type can have some other collation OID, if one was specified for the domain.

columns.name: typdefaultbin
columns.description: If typdefaultbin is not null, it is the nodeToString() representation of a default expression for the type. This is only used for domains.

columns.name: typdefault
columns.description: typdefault is null if the type has no associated default value. If typdefaultbin is not null, typdefault must contain a human-readable version of the default expression represented by typdefaultbin. If typdefaultbin is null and typdefault is not, then typdefault is the external representation of the type's default value, which can be fed to the type's input converter to produce a constant.

columns.name: typacl
columns.description: Access privileges; see and for details

columns.name: typalign

When multiple values are stored consecutively, such as in the representation of a complete row on disk, padding is inserted before a datum of this type so that it begins on the specified boundary. The alignment reference is the beginning of the first datum in the sequence. Possible values are: c = char alignment, i.e., no alignment needed.

columns.name: typstorage

columns.name: typndims

columns.name: typcollation

columns.name: typlen
columns.description: For a fixed-size type, typlen is the number of bytes in the internal representation of the type. But for a variable-length type, typlen is negative. -1 indicates a varlena type (one that has a length word), -2 indicates a null-terminated C string.

columns.name: typbyval
columns.description: typbyval determines whether internal routines pass a value of this type by value or by reference. typbyval had better be false if typlen is not 1, 2, or 4 (or 8 on machines where Datum is 8 bytes). Variable-length types are always passed by reference. Note that typbyval can be false even if the length would allow pass-by-value.

columns.name: typtype
columns.description: typtype is b for a base type, c for a composite type (e.g., a table's row type), d for a domain, e for an enum type, p for a pseudo-type, or r for a range type. See also typrelid and typbasetype.

columns.name: typdelim

columns.name: typrelid

columns.name: typelem
columns.description: If typelem is not 0 then it identifies another row in pg_type. The current type can then be subscripted like an array yielding values of type typelem. A true array type is variable length (typlen = -1), but some fixed-length (typlen > 0) types also have nonzero typelem, for example name and point.
